items.q: Tearing, photophobic infant with enlarged hazy cornea most likely has what?
o: Primary congenital glaucoma needing early goniotomy
items.exp: Trabeculodysgenesis raises pressure stretching elastic globe (buphthalmos) with Haab striae; drops bridge only to angle surgery under anaesthesia. Cataract whitens without enlargement.
r: Incorrect. Cataract lacks tearing and enlargement.
Incorrect. Tumour fills with white reflex.
items.kp: Big tearing hazy baby eye: congenital glaucoma.

items.q: Haab striae in congenital glaucoma represent what?
o: Breaks in Descemet membrane from corneal stretching
items.exp: Pressure expands infant cornea tearing Descemet endothelial layer into curvilinear lines; clearing follows pressure control unlike dystrophies. Adult corneas scar instead of stretching.
items.kp: Striae on baby cornea: stretched Descemet.

items.q: Child on potent topical steroids for vernal disease needs which surveillance?
o: Scheduled intraocular pressure checks for steroid response
items.exp: Responders spike within weeks risking silent cupping; pressure monitoring with steroid sparing switch preserves vision. Potency and duration drive risk.
items.kp: Steroid drops: check pressure on schedule.

items.q: White dandruff like flakes on lens with poor dilation and weak zonules in elderly indicates what?
o: Pseudoexfoliation with glaucoma and cataract surgery risk
items.exp: Fibrillar material clogs trabeculum and frays zonules (phacodonesis, lens subluxation risk); wide pressure swings need control and surgeons plan capsular support. Pupil refuses to dilate fully.
items.kp: Flaky lens, stiff pupil, wobbly zonules: pseudoexfoliation.

items.q: Painful blind eye with rubeosis iridis 3 months after central retinal vein occlusion is which glaucoma?
o: Neovascular (100 day) glaucoma needing panretinal photocoagulation
items.exp: Ischaemia drives anterior segment new vessels zipping angle shut; PRP ablates drive while tubes palliate pressure (filtration bleeds). Anti VEGF bridges to laser.
items.kp: New iris vessels plus rock pressure post vein block: laser retina.

items.q: Krukenberg spindle with exercise induced pigment storms in young myopic men suggests what?
o: Pigment dispersion syndrome with reverse pupillary block
items.exp: Iris concavity liberates pigment clogging trabeculum after exertion; laser iridotomy flattens configuration while pressure control prevents conversion to pigmentary glaucoma.
items.kp: Spindle pigment plus sport spikes: dispersion.

items.q: Angle recession glaucoma after blunt trauma is detected and followed how?
o: Gonioscopy for cleft with lifelong pressure surveillance
items.exp: Torn ciliary face scars months to years later; baseline gonioscopy with annual pressures catches late rises. Steroids complicate with response overlap.
r: Correct. Scope angle, watch for life.
items.kp: Knocked eye: scope the angle, watch pressure forever.

items.q: Ghost cell glaucoma follows vitreous haemorrhage by which mechanism?
o: Degenerate khaki ghost cells clogging trabecular meshwork weeks later
items.exp: Rigid haemoglobin laden cells resist egress after vitrectomy or trauma; anterior chamber washout with vitrectomy clears while pressure bridges medically.
items.kp: Old blood cells blocking drain weeks later: ghost cells.

items.q: Aniridia threatens vision through which combined mechanisms?
o: Glaucoma with foveal hypoplasia, nystagmus and cataract needing lifelong surveillance
items.exp: PAX6 haploinsufficiency arrests angle, fovea and lens development (with Wilms tumour risk in WAGR deletions); pressure, refraction and amblyopia care run together with systemic genetics.
items.kp: Missing iris plus dancing eyes: PAX6, watch pressure for life.

items.q: Aqueous misdirection (malignant) glaucoma after surgery is recognised and treated how?
o: Uniformly shallow central chamber with high pressure; cycloplegics with vitrectomy patterns
items.exp: Aqueous pockets behind vitreous pushing everything forward despite patent iridotomy; atropine tightens zonules while vitrectomy with hyaloidotomy restores forward flow.
r: Incorrect. No pus or pain pattern.
items.kp: Flat throughout after surgery with high pressure: misdirection.
